dedupe_keys.name: storm surge resilience of the drax biomass fuel supply chain through uk ports immingham hull liverpool tyne

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Drax Power made its biomass fuel supply chain resilient to storm surge. Drax runs six boilers with a maximum of 3,945 MW, three burning wood pellets imported largely from the United States. UKCP09 projected sea-level rise of up to 0.75 m along UK coasts in a century with more surge events, and during the 2013 surge the port of Immingham lost power in areas after substations flooded. Measures include raising plant equipment above surge levels, sea walls at the Immingham terminal, surge barriers on tunnels, an outer lock gate upgraded from 1 in 20 to 1 in 1,000 year protection, diesel trains that do not rely on vulnerable cables, and a multi-port strategy on both coasts with terminals at Immingham, Hull, Liverpool and Tyne. Drax invested 135 million pounds at Immingham, the port 4.7 million in the new gate and 0.5 million on substation flood works, and import capacity reached up to 2 million tonnes a year. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML. Coverage is the United Kingdom. Caveats: the climate and biodiversity benefits of biomass are disputed, and the EEA takes no position. It illustrates fuel supply chain exposure of power plants to coastal hazards for hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies. Related records: case_study-national-grid-substation-flood-defence-framework covers substation flooding.
name: Storm surge resilience of the Drax biomass fuel supply chain through UK ports (Immingham, Hull, Liverpool, Tyne)
outcomes: Equipment was raised, sea walls and surge barriers built, the Immingham outer lock gate upgraded from 1 in 20 to 1 in 1,000 year protection, and supply split across several ports, allowing up to 2 million tonnes a year of pellet imports.
